gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-mongolian: Gabarito draws every curve as if with a single nib, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. And Noto Sans Mongolian takes over with flared terminals, a modern sans that keeps things plain where the heading gets expressive.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-new-tai-lue: Gabarito looks like bent paperclip wire, with no thick-thin shifts anywhere in its expressive letters. But Noto Sans New Tai Lue is the plain sans partner, its round letters cupped rather than clenched, which makes the two feel distinct yet friendly.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-nko: Noto Sans NKo brings modern, see-through openings to the text, while Gabarito above it keeps every stroke at the same gauge in a display voice. Paragraphs would read lightly.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-nko-unjoine: Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans NKo Unjoined, whose small letters have wide openings and a gentle manner. But Gabarito above it has a pipe-cleaner feel in every letterform, so a long page would settle into easy, unhurried reading.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-old-south-a: Wire-bright and bold-faced, Gabarito keeps constant-width arms and legs, while Noto Sans Old South Arabian lets its curved strokes end before turning inward. Longer text would feel clean and friendly.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-sans-shavian: Gabarito's letters look drawn with a round-tipped pen, open at the terminals so the counters flow outward. Noto Sans Shavian is its loose-curved, clean sans counterpart, and that pairing of expressive and tidy is what holds them together.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-ojuju: Ojuju reads like lightly flexed spring wire, with wide s curves barely curled in and modest contrast you notice only up close. Gabarito, with identical vertical and horizontal weight, makes long reading feel brisk.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-palanquin: Gabarito's curves never thin out at the turns, and its terminals are cut open for a one-nib look. Palanquin's wide, unclosed curved letters give it a contemporary sans body, and that lively-against-composed tension is the pair's real strength.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-philosopher: Gabarito's round letters look bent from wire. It does expressive display work best, while Philosopher, a plain sans with soft shifts in thickness and plenty of daylight inside its curves, handles the text.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-pontano-sans: Gabarito has no thick or thin parts in any letter. Shrink that heading, or enlarge Pontano Sans, and the sans-serif's wide open c terminals start to match the heading's open, expressive build.
